items.line: Netflix announces "Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure", a new series set for 2028, with the line "Before Hawkins, there was Marion." Fans reply in the thread.

Thomas Massie asks Grok whether F-35 jets flew over a Washington press conference about Epstein and drowned out survivors who were speaking. Grok is made by xAI, which also makes the model that gathers this site’s posts. Not checked here.

The White House account quotes a statement from President Trump saying the stock market had one of its worst days because of the election results and blaming Democrats for drops in 401(k)s. Not checked here.
gloccnim says they did not realise how well their parents raised them until they were around other people. The post has attached media.
KoomseFN shares the loot route their squad took to get the Pirate Token, saying it yields over 400 chests a game. A video is attached.
LegionHoops reports that Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd announced on the Fudd Around Pod that they have broken up.
frankiebyler_ tells Taylor Swift her album is at Goodwill for $1.99, saying they walked in and saw it. A photo or video is attached. Not checked here.
kchartsmaster reports that NCT DREAM released a music video teaser for "Boogie Woogie".
Gabriele_Corno posts attached media with the caption "Sometimes all you need is an outside cat to show some love".

Kaitlan Collins reports that Trump announces Stephen Miller will become his chief of staff. The White House posts Trump’s statement: Miller starts Monday, November 9, and Susie Wiles moves to the Trump Political Operation.
WarMonitor3 says Iran is starting to hand out iodine tablets to residents near nuclear sites, and reads it as a sign that large strikes could be coming. Not checked here.
nicksortor says three police officers were shot just outside Denver, Colorado, and that their conditions were unknown when it posted early on November 6 (UTC). Not checked here.
WatcherGuru says Japan’s Nikkei 225 has officially entered a bear market as stocks fall. Not checked here.
Polymarket says Mamdani proposes banning Amazon from using third-party delivery contractors, so it would have to hire drivers directly. Not checked here.
Discord shows a side-by-side test on mobile: its current Android app on the left and a new version it is building in Rust on the right.
Elon Musk invites people to "join the Terafab project" if they want to iterate fast with radically new chip designs. The post does not say what Terafab is or who runs it.

US Central Command says the State Department's Rewards for Justice program offers up to $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran's nuclear program, its facilities, equipment and personnel.
Cash App replies to a user that it does not condone violence of any kind and is no longer a sponsor of "this podcast". The post does not name the podcast or say why. Not checked here.

tradingchik says Clinton lost 54 House seats in 1994, Obama 63 in 2010 and Trump 41 in 2026, and that this is not the historic event critics claim. The 2026 figure is the poster's and has not been checked here.
NASA shows the sunshade that will fly on NEO Surveyor, a spacecraft meant to spot nearby asteroids and comets that ground-based telescopes might miss.

Igor Bobic reports that Chris Murphy is out of the hospital. Quoting Murphy, he says Murphy was diagnosed with a small bleed in the thalamus region of his brain and will spend several weeks at a rehabilitation center.
Susie Wiles says today is her last day as White House Chief of Staff. She calls the job the honor of a lifetime and says her role may be changing.
Elon Musk says Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for more Cybercab production. NBC News reports the same.

Peter Daou says it is staggering to see a conversation like this on corporate US media, and that a Morning Joe panel was gobsmacked by Abdul El-Sayed’s points. The post carries a video clip he credits to Drop Site News; the capture does not describe it.
DiscussingFilm shares the first trailer for a LEGO Ninjago anime series, which it says releases in 2027.
PopBase, an entertainment news account, says Macklemore has named nine venues that declined to host his “FREE PALESTINE” tour, starting with Madison Square Garden. Not checked here.
spectatorindex posts a “BREAKING” claim that over $3 trillion in value has been wiped from the US stock market that day. Not checked here.
Fabrizio Romano quotes PSG’s João Neves, who told Canal Plus that a move to Spain or England is not a goal for him and that he is happy in Paris.
Tesla says it is launching in Argentina later this month. The attached post from @Tesla_LatAm, in Spanish, gives the date as 20 November.

SpaceX announces what it calls the first orbital Starship launch carrying advanced Starlink satellites, and points to a film, "Go For Orbit". Elon Musk's quote of it says the next flight will try to catch both the booster and Starship.

A post says a small dibbler named Steve at Perth Zoo helped save his endangered species without having young, by serving as the first male that females met in breeding trials. The post says this is according to the zoo. Not checked here.

Anthropic announces an Engineering Blog post on how "dreaming" helps Claude organize what it has learned and correct its mistakes. Claude is made by Anthropic, which also makes the model that writes this page.

An account that follows the Strait of Hormuz says a US fighter jet struck an Iranian surface-to-air missile launcher on Qeshm Island after an Iranian missile was launched at it, citing initial reports and Iranian state media. Not checked here.
Rep. Nancy Mace says "we will NOT be putting pronouns in our bio or email signature."
An account named duke asks whether it is illegal to walk into any random university and attend lectures.
Ian Rapoport reports, citing sources, that Seahawks guard Quenton Nelson will have knee surgery to clean out cartilage, with a timeline of a few weeks, and that the plan is to avoid Injured Reserve.
Slangtongue lists artists, musicians, coders, writers, managers and researchers who each say AI sucks, then adds a person who cannot do any of those things saying it is the best tool ever.
Borys Kit says multiple sources told The Hollywood Reporter that Robert Pattinson is one of the men who screen tested for James Bond. DiscussingFilm’s post, attached, says the same. Not checked here.
BBC News reports that Elon Musk appears to signal the end of the road for the Cybertruck, and links to its story.
SportsCenter posts a video and says Valparaiso beat Purdue at the buzzer in double overtime.
spectatorindex posts a “BREAKING” claim that Paraguay’s president has resigned after a bank collapse left millions of people without access to their accounts. Not checked here.

ESPN reports that Kristaps Porzingis announced he is stepping away from basketball to put his health first. It says he told fans his body has not responded as he expected and that he will work with the Warriors on a solution. Not checked here.
The official World of Warcraft account says its WoW: Forever launch was the biggest in the game’s history by peak concurrent players, with the most returning players ever. Not checked here.
GoNintendoTweet reports that Shigeru Miyamoto was absent from Nintendo's investor Q&A because of a "sudden health issue" and is in stable condition. Not checked here.
